**Reflection (Required)**  
*\*Feel free to skip these for now and come back after you’ve completed the project\!\**

| 🤔 Reflection Question \#1: The traversal let the service read files your own account couldn't. What gave the service more access than you? |
| :---- |
| The FTP service runs as root, and the student account does not. `cat /etc/shadow` and `cat /opt/wishful-thinking/real_earnings.txt` both returned Permission denied. The server opens whatever path it is given with its own privileges, so a traversal request is read as root. That privilege gap is what let the service return files the student shell cannot open. |

| 🧠 Reflection Question \#2: You wrote a rule, then beat it with URL-encoding. What does that tell you about trusting a single signature? |
| :---- |
| A signature only matches the exact bytes it was written for. `content:"../"` fired on the literal traversal in `server.pcapng`, but the same climb sent as `%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2fetc/shadow` still came back HTTP 200 with the root line of `/etc/shadow`. The server URL-decodes the path before it opens the file, so the exploit works and the literal rule stays silent. One content match is not coverage of the attack. |

#### 

| Detection rule: Your local.rules rule line \+ one alert\_fast line showing it fired 4× on the capture. |
| :---- |
| Rule in `/usr/local/etc/rules/local.rules`: `alert tcp any any -> any 8888 ( msg:"Directory traversal (../ in a request)"; flow:to_server,established; content:"../"; sid:1000002; rev:1; )` Fired 4 times on `server.pcapng`. One line: `07/26-21:40:08.059778 [**] [1:1000002:1] "Directory traversal (../ in a request)" [**] [Priority: 0] {TCP} 127.0.0.1:59668 -> 127.0.0.1:8888` |
| **Notes** (Optional)**:** The same signature also fired at 07/26-21:40:08.089675 (59670), 07/26-21:40:08.119151 (59686), and 07/26-21:40:08.149591 (59702). |

```
alert tcp any any -> any 8888 ( msg:"Directory traversal (../ in a request)"; flow:to_server,established; content:"../"; sid:1000002; rev:1; )
```

```

07/26-21:40:08.089675 [**] [1:1000002:1] "Directory traversal (../ in a request)" [**] [Priority: 0] {TCP} 127.0.0.1:59670 -> 127.0.0.1:8888
07/26-21:40:08.119151 [**] [1:1000002:1] "Directory traversal (../ in a request)" [**] [Priority: 0] {TCP} 127.0.0.1:59686 -> 127.0.0.1:8888
```

#### 

| Breach scope: The files the attacker reached in server.pcapng, with the ones outside the FTP folder marked. |
| :---- |
| 7 requests in `server.pcapng`. 6 were served (HTTP 200) and 1 missed (HTTP 404). Of the 6 served, 4 are `../` hits outside the FTP folder. Served inside the folder: `/general/reports.txt`, `/general/budget.txt`. Served OUTSIDE the folder: `/etc/os-release`, `/etc/shadow`, `/opt/northwind/real_earnings.txt`, `/etc/passwd`. Missed: `/nonexistent.txt` (404). |
| **Notes** (Optional)**:** Read with `tcpdump -qns 0 -A -r /opt/snort-lab/project/server.pcapng`. The captured attacker used `/opt/northwind/real_earnings.txt`, which is a different path from the live lab file at `/opt/wishful-thinking/real_earnings.txt`. |

| # | Request | Status | Outside the FTP folder? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `GET /general/reports.txt` | 200 OK | No. Public folder. |
| 2 | `GET /general/budget.txt` | 200 OK | No. Public folder. |
| 3 | `GET /../../../etc/os-release` | 200 OK | **Yes. Traversal.** |
| 4 | `GET /../../../etc/shadow` | 200 OK | **Yes. Traversal.** |
| 5 | `GET /../../../opt/northwind/real_earnings.txt` | 200 OK | **Yes. Traversal.** |
| 6 | `GET /../../../etc/passwd` | 200 OK | **Yes. Traversal.** |
| 7 | `GET /nonexistent.txt` | 404 Not Found | Not served. |

#### 

| Remediation: The server-side fix that stops it at the source \+ one defense-in-depth measure. |
| :---- |
| **Stop it at the source.** The service builds the file path as the FTP root plus the request path, URL-decodes it, and opens the result with no check for `..`. After decoding, resolve the path and reject the request unless the resolved path is still inside `/home/student/ftp_folder`. Return 400 or 403 instead of opening it. That blocks both literal `../` and `%2e%2e%2f`, because the check happens after decoding. **Contain the damage anyway.** Do not run this service as root. Run it as an unprivileged user that cannot read `/etc/shadow` or the root-only earnings file (mode 600, root-owned). The capture reached os-release, shadow, passwd, and a confidential earnings file only because the process had root's read access. A dropped privilege would have kept a missed path check from handing those files out. |
| **Notes** (Optional)**:**  |

**Stretch Challenge (Optional)**

| Beat your own rule: The URL-encoded (%2e%2e%2f) bypass \+ a second rule that catches the encoded form. |
| :---- |
| Bypass request: `http://localhost:8888/%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2fetc/shadow` returned HTTP 200 and `root:*:20675:0:99999:7:::`. Those bytes are `%2e%2e%2f`, not `../`, so the literal rule does not match. Second rule: `alert tcp any any -> any 8888 ( msg:"Directory traversal (URL-encoded ../)"; flow:to_server,established; content:"%2e%2e%2f"; nocase; sid:1000003; rev:1; )` |
| **Notes** (Optional)**:** The encoded request was sent with `node attack.js` inside the lab container and the service decoded it before opening `/etc/shadow`. `nocase` is there because `%2E%2E%2F` is the same encoding in uppercase. |

```
alert tcp any any -> any 8888 ( msg:"Directory traversal (URL-encoded ../)"; flow:to_server,established; content:"%2e%2e%2f"; nocase; sid:1000003; rev:1; )
```
